object_description: elongated single-story building with a broad canopy
design_condition: Placed along Welschmattstrasse, the low building remains subordinate to the existing school, preserves spatial connections through the site, and frames a connected longitudinal outdoor space, but its large footprint reduces tree retention.

positive.statement: The child-friendly scale makes the building subordinate to the existing school building as a serving element.

position.rationale: Low elongated mass and horizontal elevations show a subordinate, child-scaled building volume.

positive.statement: The tree-lined, connected and longitudinal outdoor space is given great importance.

position.rationale: Open space is approximated alongside the elongated building footprint toward the southern end.

positive.statement: The precise positioning and contemporary independent expression fit the existing context.

position.rationale: Distinctive elongated canopy geometry is visible as an independent linear form.

positive.statement: The visually covered outdoor area ties the school rooms together.

position.rationale: Parallel longitudinal edges and layered elevations identify the central covered connecting zone.

positive.statement: The structural lighting on both sides provides daylight to the school rooms.

position.rationale: Two long sides are visible, but lighting elements are not individually distinguishable in the sample.

positive.statement: The internal division is detached from the basic structure and is flexible.

position.rationale: Interior organization is not exposed; marker is constrained to the building’s central longitudinal surface.

positive.statement: The project has a comparatively small volume and little floor space and can therefore be classified as economical.

position.rationale: The sampled form is a relatively narrow, low-rise elongated volume.

positive.statement: The investment costs are favorable compared to the other award-winning projects.

position.rationale: Cost comparison has no useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: The large footprint cannot comply with the tree protection requirements, retaining only a third of the meadow areas.

position.rationale: The elongated footprint occupies much of the visible site-side plan area.

negative.statement: The building structure is not optimally integrated into the precise path network.

position.rationale: Path relationships are not distinguishable; marker is placed at the building’s north-west approach.

negative.statement: The organization and development of the additive spatial structure are not optimally solved.

position.rationale: Internal additive organization is inferred within the elongated central building region.

negative.statement: The adjoining uses are not optimally developed or sufficiently separated, and the individual entrances are too small.

position.rationale: Entrances are unmarked; approximate marker uses the exposed south-east end.

negative.statement: The static construction is likely to be cost-intensive.

position.rationale: Structure is not separable from the sampled envelope, so it is anchored centrally within the building.

negative.statement: The building is not very compact due to its single-story structure and dimensions.

position.rationale: Long footprint and low horizontal profile visibly indicate limited compactness.

negative.statement: It is questionable whether the proposed materialization could achieve Minergie-P-ECO.

position.rationale: Certification feasibility is a non-spatial performance judgment.
